intro: Daniel Okoye is the endpoint administrator at Brightline Distribution, which has warehouses, an office, and an ever-growing pile of laptops, phones and kiosks. Right now every new device is set up by hand by whoever has a free afternoon. Daniel’s boss wants that changed this year. MD-102 is the toolkit.
Follow Daniel as he moves Brightline from hand-built devices to a managed fleet.

device-provisioning-updates: Two hundred identical laptops are arriving for warehouse kiosks. They should switch on, sign in and set themselves up with nobody touching them. Fifteen executive laptops should be prepared by a partner before they are couriered out. Daniel learns the provisioning options for each, and how to roll out Windows updates in waves so the first group finds problems before everyone else does.
prepare-identity-infrastructure: Brightline’s regional help desks should see and manage only their own region’s devices. Daniel learns how to decide who manages devices, how devices join the directory in different ways, how groups can fill themselves, and how to tag things so each team sees only its own. He also sorts out which kinds of enrolment are allowed.
protect-devices-and-access: Security wants a five-day grace period for ordinary compliance failures, but a device flagged as high risk should lose access at once. Daniel learns how compliance policy, risk signals and sign-in rules work together, how encryption and baseline settings are applied, and how to stop apps from running with more rights than they need.
manage-secure-applications: Field technicians will read company email on their own phones. Daniel must allow one approved mail app, block the generic one, and be able to wipe only the company data if a phone is lost. He learns the difference between pushing an app out, offering it, and removing it, how to protect data inside apps, and how certificates and remote help fit in.
optimize-endpoint-operations: The same background service keeps stopping on a handful of laptops, and the help desk only hears when someone is annoyed. Daniel learns to detect the problem on a schedule, fix it automatically, and report on how healthy the fleet is overall. He also scripts the repetitive work, and sets alerts so that he hears first.

epilogue: By the end of the year Daniel’s fleet builds itself, stays patched, and tells him when something is wrong. On exam day he treats each question as an everyday decision: which tool, for which devices, with which settings, for which people.

device-provisioning-updates: Daniel assigns a user-driven profile to the warehouse kiosks. The first kiosk arrives and waits for someone to sign in. Nobody is going to sign in; it is a kiosk. It sits at a login screen, glowing, like a very patient lighthouse. A self-deploying profile was what the job required.
prepare-identity-infrastructure: Daniel creates a dynamic group for new laptops and targets a critical setup with it. The group takes a few minutes to catch up, and the first batch of laptops sets up without the settings. He learns that things that need to apply the moment a device is provisioned should not rely on something that updates a little later.
protect-devices-and-access: Daniel marks devices noncompliant immediately, with no grace period. The first morning, forty people are locked out for a missing update. The help desk phone sounds like a smoke alarm. A five-day grace window is the polite version of the same policy, and the one he deploys the next week.
manage-secure-applications: Daniel packages a Win32 app and leaves out the detection rule, ‘to save time’. Intune cannot tell whether the app is installed, so it keeps trying. And trying. The app is installed on every laptop eleven times, which is ten more than anyone wanted.
optimize-endpoint-operations: A colleague sees a lost personal phone and presses ‘Wipe’. The phone, which also held the owner’s wedding photos, is now very clean. The correct action for a personal device was to retire it, removing the company data and nothing else. The colleague apologises, in person, with a coffee.

device-provisioning-updates.problem: Setting up and updating devices by hand takes too long and is inconsistent.
device-provisioning-updates.cause: Each device is built individually, and updates reach everyone at once.
device-provisioning-updates.solution: Autopilot, Windows 365, update rings and Autopatch automate setup and stage updates.
device-provisioning-updates.next: Next, preparing the identity and infrastructure behind devices.

prepare-identity-infrastructure.problem: Devices enrol incorrectly or are managed by the wrong people.
prepare-identity-infrastructure.cause: Directory, licensing and group settings were not prepared first.
prepare-identity-infrastructure.solution: MDM authority, enrolment limits, join types, groups and scope tags set the foundation.
prepare-identity-infrastructure.next: Next, protecting devices and gating access.

protect-devices-and-access.cause: Nothing checks the device’s health before granting access.
protect-devices-and-access.solution: Compliance policies, Conditional Access, Defender risk, baselines and encryption combine into access decisions.

manage-secure-applications.problem: Apps are installed inconsistently and company data leaks on personal devices.
manage-secure-applications.cause: Apps are managed by hand and device and data protection are mixed up.
manage-secure-applications.solution: Deployment intents, app protection, configuration policies, certificates and remote help manage and protect apps.

optimize-endpoint-operations.problem: Problems are fixed one ticket at a time, and the fleet’s health is unknown.
optimize-endpoint-operations.cause: Support is reactive, and repetitive tasks are manual.
optimize-endpoint-operations.solution: Graph automation, remediation scripts, analytics, alerts and the right actions on lost devices make operations proactive.
optimize-endpoint-operations.next: That completes the lessons. Next come the cheat sheet, the word bank and the practice questions.
